submissions.title: Governor Abbott Directs Comprehensive Data Center Audit
submissions.excerpt: Directed PUCT and ERCOT to conduct a comprehensive verification and audit of every data center interconnection request.
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: Gov. Abbott ordered PUCT/ERCOT to audit every project in the ERCOT interconnection queue (~474 GW requested, ~90% from data centers) before allowing grid connection; projects that fail to comply must be denied. This is a grid-interconnection (site power) basis, not IT load, and no individual project's disclosed MW/capex changes yet. It affects essentially every Texas project this tracker follows as UNDER_CONSTRUCTION/ANNOUNCED (Stargate Milam/Shackelford, Sweetwater, Abilene, Pecos, Hall County/Lancium, Compass Meridian, Freestone, etc.), so I'm submitting it as a general restriction rather than attaching it to one project — a reviewer may want to log it against each affected project individually. Caveat: WebFetch to primary/news sources was unavailable in this session (network policy blocked it, including gov.texas.gov itself); the excerpt above is reconstructed from WebSearch result snippets across multiple outlets (Houston Public Media, Texas Tribune, KSAT, Community Impact) rather than a direct fetch of the press release text, so please verify the exact wording against the source before treating it as CONFIRMED.

submissions.title: This Nevada city is appealing a federally-approved data center it tried to reject
submissions.excerpt: Boulder City's appeal says BLM did not consult the city or allow adequate public input before approving the project.
submissions.suggestedProjectName: Townsite Data Center (Boulder City, NV — Skylar Capital Management)
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION / new project not yet tracked. First data center ever approved on BLM federal public land: BLM approved it in June 2026 by reusing a prior solar-project authorization on the same parcel, without a fresh environmental review or public comment period. Boulder City Council voted unanimously on July 14 to appeal; the Center for Biological Diversity and Sierra Club Toiyabe Chapter filed a separate administrative appeal on July 27. Reported water use is ~560 acre-feet/yr versus 25 acre-feet/yr under the original solar approval it was permitted through. In response, U.S. Rep. Rashida Tlaib introduced H.R. 9939, the No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act. Caveat: WebFetch was unavailable this session so I could not pull the article's exact text directly; the 167 MW figure and quote above come from WebSearch snippets aggregating this UPR piece with Las Vegas Review-Journal, Newsweek, and Center for Biological Diversity coverage — please re-verify against the primary article before treating either as CONFIRMED.

claims.methodology: Project capacity as reported in secondary news coverage of the BLM approval; not independently verified against a primary filing this session

submissions.title: Paducah DOE site picked for AI, computing campus, including power generation and storage
submissions.excerpt: The Energy Department selected the Paducah site for an AI data center, including power generation and storage.
submissions.note: New project, not yet tracked. DOE selected its former Paducah Gaseous Diffusion Plant (uranium-enrichment) site in western Kentucky for a 2 GW federal AI/computing campus with on-site power generation and storage, announced at a DOE press conference on July 29; targeting 2028 completion. A ~$100B capex figure appears in some secondary coverage (e.g. Tech Times) but I could not confirm it against a DOE primary source this session (WebFetch to gov/DOE sites was unavailable) — recommend leaving capex blank or LOW confidence until a reviewer checks the DOE release directly. This is distinct from the separate, still-unsigned ~$250-500B Nvidia/OpenAI talks over a 10 GW site at the nearby Pike County, Ohio PORTS site (SB Energy/SoftBank) — I excluded that one as still MOU/talks-stage per the submission rules, not yet announced as final by a principal party.

claims.methodology: DOE-announced capacity for the Paducah site, per news coverage of the July 29 press conference

submissions.title: Tech giant OpenAI plans to build $20 billion data center near Georgia coast
submissions.excerpt: Georgia Power will provide the data center with 3.2 gigawatts of energy, delivered in phases from 2028 to 2032.
submissions.note: New project, not yet tracked. OpenAI's first self-built Georgia campus ('Project Camellia'), 1,400+ acres in Effingham County's Savannah Gateway Industrial Hub near Savannah. $20B capex; 3.2 GW power committed by Georgia Power delivered in phases 2028-2032 (site/grid basis, not confirmed IT load). ECIDA approved a 50% property tax abatement for 15 years. Opens in phases starting 2028, projected 400 jobs rising to 1,000 by 2032.

claims.methodology: Capex as stated in company/local news coverage of the OpenAI Effingham County announcement
Georgia Power-committed capacity per news coverage, phased 2028-2032; site/grid power, not confirmed as IT load

submissions.title: County Announces Pause on New Data Center Development Following Maryland Supreme Court Decision
submissions.excerpt: Executive order pauses acceptance and processing of new applications until December 31, after the State issues its Report.
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: Frederick County Executive Jessica Fitzwater signed an executive order on July 1 pausing acceptance/processing of new Critical Digital Infrastructure (data center) and substation applications through Dec 31, 2026, pending Maryland's statewide Data Center Impact Analysis and Report. It came a day after the Maryland Supreme Court rejected a 20,000-signature referendum petition on the county's data-center zoning overlay (the Carrollton Manor / CDI-OZ area north of Adamstown). A related, narrower land-use vote on including Rural Legacy Area land within that overlay was separately paused by the Executive on July 30 pending further study (per WYPR, 2026-07-30). Frederick joins Prince George's, Montgomery and Baltimore Counties, which adopted their own MD pauses in recent weeks — not separately submitted here since those are now 3-4 weeks old and outside this run's freshness window; a reviewer may still want them for completeness. Caveat: WebFetch to the primary county source was unavailable this session; excerpt reconstructed from WebSearch snippets (WFMD, Maryland Daily Record, WYPR) rather than a direct fetch — please verify exact wording.
